judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The unselected 'Portarias' tab of the Documentos quicktabs. The live stylesheet sets 'ul.quicktabs-tabs.quicktabs-style-zen li a {color:#777; background:#eee}' (only li.active gets white on green), and the screenshot pixels at the element's bounds are #777777 on #eeeeee, 3.86:1. At 16px weight 600 it is not large text (bold needs 18.66px), and an operable tab is not an inactive component, so 4.5:1 applies and fails. Reasons I tested that do not hold: the 'Alto contraste' switcher (G174) would make these tabs white on #2a2a2a, but the switcher link itself is white 11.2px on #009045 (4.14:1), its script compares the id 'is_normal_contrast' against the served 'is-normal-contrast' so the first activation does nothing, and the high-contrast sheet leaves the search placeholder at 2.92:1, so G174's three checks are not met. Live HTML and CSS match the capture.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'English' link of the language switcher in a page with lang='pt-br'. It carries only xml:lang='en'; the page is served as text/html (checked the response header), where the HTML spec says an xml:lang attribute in no namespace has no effect on language processing, and Blink and Gecko only read xml:lang in the XML namespace, so the link inherits pt-br. Understanding 3.1.2 says single words count unless it is not clear a change of language was intended; here the change is plainly intended (the author even wrote xml:lang), 'English' is not the Portuguese word (inglês) and is not a proper name used across languages untranslated. The live HTML is identical to the capture.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The header search textbox. Its associated label holds the junk text '«nenhum»' ('none') and is display:none (.views-exposed-form label), and a script adds placeholder='Pesquisar'. Chrome's tree in the capture gives the name '' with a labelledby relation to that hidden label: the empty label wins and the placeholder is not used, so in Chrome the field has no accessible name (ACT e086e5 fails), which is what the claim says. But a concrete counter-reading holds up: HTML-AAM falls through to the placeholder when the label yields no usable text, ACT e086e5 Passed Example 5 accepts a placeholder as the name, axe-core's label rule passes a non-empty placeholder, accname 1.2 would even take the hidden label's '«nenhum»', and Chrome still exposes the placeholder, which major screen readers announce, so 'announces only textbox' is overstated. Whether this fails 4.1.2 or only 3.3.2/2.4.6 is something competent auditors would split on. The live HTML, CSS and script match the capture.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The title 'Unipampa | Universidade Federal do Pampa' is on the university portal's home page (https://unipampa.edu.br/portal/), whose h1 is the Unipampa logo. For a home page the site and organisation name is exactly its topic and purpose, so the title identifies the page and 2.4.2 is met (F25 is not triggered). The claim that it 'says nothing about this page' is false. The model had the URL and the title and judged wrongly. The live title is the same.
